baseline.description: A perturbation changes expression by the sum of its genes' single-gene changes in training (additive model).

lineage.hypothesis: RIDGE on the baseline features plus the built-in sum of each target gene's single-gene training change.
For a perturbation p and gene g, the average control co-expression between g and p's target genes predicts delta[p,g].
The Replogle CRISPRi screen delta (sign-adjusted) for gene g under perturbation p is a strong predictor of the CRISPRa response.
Drop control_mean from the best model (EXP_0025) to test whether it still earns its place.
Drop mean_response from the best model (EXP_0039) to test whether it still earns its place.
The average delta of gene g across training perturbations whose target gene sets are similar to p (measured by Jaccard similarity of target gene sets) predicts delta[p,g].
A feature that weights each target gene's replogle delta by its co-expression with gene g will outperform the simple average replogle delta.
A feature that weights training perturbation deltas by inverse PPI network distance between target gene sets will capture functional similarity.
The average training delta of gene g under perturbations whose targets are direct PPI neighbors of p's targets is predictive of delta[p,g].
The average sign-adjusted Replogle delta of PPI neighbors of p's targets predicts delta[p,g] because neighboring genes in the network may respond similarly in the CRISPRi screen.
Multiplying the sign-adjusted Replogle delta by a PPI-distance decay term from the perturbation target improves prediction over the raw Replogle feature.
A weighted average of training deltas using inverse PPI distance (1/d) instead of exponential decay captures long-range effects better.
Tuning ridge regularization alpha for the current best feature set may improve performance. [sweep alpha_grid=10000]
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=10000 for the best model (EXP_0210).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=30000 for the best model (EXP_0218).
Drop ppi_inverse_distance_response_e182 from the best model (EXP_0235) to test whether it still earns its place.
After adding the missing helpful features, the optimal ridge alpha may shift; sweeping alpha could improve performance. [sweep alpha_grid=130000]
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=130000 for the best model (EXP_0407).
Optimizing ridge alpha over a broader range (e.g., 1e5 to 1e6) improves the current best score. [sweep alpha_grid=400000]
Add replogle_weighted_coexpression_v2_e101 to the best model (EXP_0439) although it did not help where it was first tried.
The optimal ridge penalty for the best feature set lies near alpha=400000, but a finer sweep can improve performance. [sweep alpha_grid=300000]

most_useful_features.description: For perturbation p and gene g, weighted average of delta[q,g] over training perturbations q, where the weight is exp(-decay * min_shortest_path_distance between any target of p and any target of q) computed from the PPI network.
Weighted average of training deltas by exp(-PPI shortest path distance) between target sets.
Jaccard-similarity-weighted average of training deltas over perturbations with similar targets.
For perturbation p and gene g, weighted average of delta[q,g] over training perturbations q (excluding p), with weights equal to the Jaccard similarity between the target gene sets of p and q.
Sign-adjusted Replogle CRISPRi screen delta for perturbation p's targets.
For perturbation p and gene g, average delta[q,g] over training perturbations q whose target set shares at least one PPI neighbor with p's targets.
For perturbation p and gene g, weighted average of delta[q,g] over training perturbations q, with weight = 1/(1+shortest_path_distance(g, target(q))).
Sum over p's target genes t of sign-adjusted Replogle delta(t) weighted by control co-expression(t, g).
Weighted average of training deltas over perturbations q, weighted by cosine similarity between node2vec embeddings of p's targets and q's targets.
For perturbation p and gene g, average delta[q,g] over training perturbations q whose targets share a PPI community with p's targets.
